full_judgment: 9. Dhaka Electric Supply Company Limited (DESCO) is a Public Limited Company registered under the Companies Act, 1994. It appears that it has been listed by the Dhaka Stock Exchange and Chittagong Stock Exchange on 18-6-2006 and that 31,77,985 Ordinary Shares of Taka 100 each were off-loaded in the two Stock Exchanges of the country and are being owned and subscribed by the public as reflected from Annexure Z to the Supplementary Affidavit of the Affidavit-in-Opposition of the respondent Nos. 2-6. This indicates that a substantial portion of the shares of DESCO Ltd. is owned by the public and that the company is being administered in accordance with the Companies Act, 1994 by keeping the corporate character and nature of the establishment. The Company's decisions, therefore, are subject to scrutiny by the share-holders who are members of the public. It cannot be said that the Company is being controlled by the Government; its decisions, therefore, cannot be subject to judicial review under Article 102 of the Constitution. Due to the corporate nature of the company there is sufficient scope for an aggrieved person to ventilate his grievance in the general meeting of the Company and through the other avenues provided by the Companies Act. The cases referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner i.e. the case of Conforce Limited vs Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited reported in 42 DLR 33 and the case of Md Abdus Sabur vs Rural Electrification Board reported in 10 BLC 502 appear to be in a different category. In both the cases Titas Gas Company Limited as well as in Rural Power Company Limited the Government has entrusted huge amount of its funds for carrying out its functions by the concerned limited companies and those limited companies were created pursuant to various statutory provisions for the performance of Governmental functions. Moreover, the shares of those companies are not traded in the stock markets of the country. In such circumstances, the Court appears to have taken the view that the functions and orders passed by the said companies were essentially those of the Government and ought to be subject to judicial review. That however, is not the case with regard to DESCO and, as such, we are of the opinion that this Writ Petition is not maintainable. The petitioner may take his case to the Civil Court for appropriate relief if so advised and in such circumstances, the time spent for filing the instant Writ Petition till the date of receipt of this order is to be disregarded for the purposes of limitation.
